title: Learning to arrange and the vocal Sing Band
summary: A Kennedy saxophonist taught him arranging; he studied harmony with Gene Page's father, and led a band imitating instruments with voices.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, did you arrange a lead? A play piano? Yes.

I played piano. And then I learned how to read. One of the saxophone players with Claude Kennedy. What is the guy's name? I think the first saxophone player. In Claude Kennedy's band. Taught me how to arrange. Taught me... And taught me something. Get the scale. Know how to scale. Know what you want to put down. Use the piano for your foundation. And these are the transpositions. Here's what you do with the saxes. Here's how you have to brass. And how to score. And how to get your intervals. And so I find out how to do that through... He, the first lead man, which was Claude, taught me. I can't think of the guy's name. But anyhow, he was very good. He taught me... Then I went to school. Then I started harmony. Then I began to learn how to read. Because that became something I had to be able to put music down. Write it. And no matter how difficult, you'd have to be able to write it yourself in order to be able to be successful. And so that was the thing that I had to learn. And then I went... I got ahead of my band. To the extent... I mean, my band got ahead of me. They got very popular at that time for playing parties. I had a six, eight-piece band. Then we were playing for dances. And then at that time, I was around. And I did all the arrangements. I was trying... I was doing some of the arrangements, but I couldn't read the scores so fast. So I had the teacher that was teaching. She would read the scores and write them down, everything around. So in the meantime, I'd learn at home and then come back, join them at night. I'd know it. But that complicated things that we played. But that was some of the way that I developed into the music. Then I began most serious. Took up harmony. I had two teachers. And then I was... Gene Page, his father, taught me a lot. His name is Gene Page, too. He's Gene Page's son. He's the best. No, Gene Page, his father, was very good. Gene Page was very fine arrangement. He raises for all the Hollywood stars out there. He's very good. He's very good. So I learned through him and through Dr. Wilkins, I think. He was another teacher. So anyway, then I began to grow and grow and grow until I began to develop into... From experience, you know, from having a band and having vocal groups and things like that. But again, they get experience from most pictures. Of course, you know, I ended up in Bing Crosby's picture. Ranger for Dick's Bing Crosby's picture. Then I got picked up a sing band that did everything with their mouths. Trumpets, the mouths. They had a brass section, saxophone section. I had a trombone section. I had a string section. I had vibraphones, slap bass. Everything that we used. And everything was, yeah. It was on the... The Mill Brothers started, but we had it. From every standpoint, like a full band. We played on Rudy Valet's show. We went in Eddie Cantor's picture. We went in Bing Crosby's. We went in the picture. When it was straight, when they had no... The strikes, you know. It was strike positions. You know, when musicians strike, Bing couldn't... I don't know the picture. We furnished the band for Bing Crosby's picture. With these guys' mouths. With singers behind us. There would be a chorus, choir. But we would have the full band with the mouths. So these guys imitating a tremendous thing. They didn't believe it. It's hard. We were on Deck of Records. It's hard to believe it. That's one way it wasn't successful. They didn't believe it was... They thought it was a band.
Well, what was the name of the band?
Sing Band. The Sing Band. It's been recorded.
Yeah. The Sing Band. I just don't happen to know that.

The Sing Band. I just don't know where they are either. The Sing Band. We did two or three sides of Deck. But they were so authentic. They were so silent. It was like a band. They couldn't sell it on the idea that it was what it was.
